newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada, U.S. fail to resolve salmon dispute.
newsitem.headline: Canada, U.S. fail to resolve salmon dispute.

text.p: Canada and the United States failed to reach agreement on Friday after contentious talks aimed at resolving a dispute over how to divide the Pacific salmon catch.
The two countries held three days of negotiations this week, their first meetings on the salmon dispute since talks collapsed in acrimony a month ago.

The two countries have squabbled for years over how to divide dwindling salmon stocks in the Pacific Northwest and several attempts at a settlement have failed. Pressure has mounted for a deal because the salmon fishing season soon gets under way in earnest.

"After three days really nothing has happened," British Columbia Premier Glen Clark told reporters after the talks adjourned, while calling for a decision to be made at the G7 summit underway in Denver.
"Canada has made historic concessions in this round. Americans are taking advantage of this."
Negotiators said they had formally agreed to suspend the talks and hoped to meet early next week.
